E) The initial X-ray demonstrates right lower lobe nodules that remain unchanged on the follow-up X-ray.
F) The initial X-ray shows right upper lobe consolidation with new left hilar consolidation in the follow-up X-ray.

facts.answer_text: The characteristic pulmonary finding pattern in Churg-Strauss Syndrome on serial chest X-rays is referred to as the "cannonball" appearance. This pattern is typically seen in the upper lobes of the lungs and is characterized by multiple, well-defined, round, and homogenous opacities.
